events.title: US consumers are muscling through higher prices, but for how long?
events.summary: High gas prices are intensifying inflation and vacuuming up more of Americans’ dollars, yet consumers are still digging deep to spend, powering the economy, at least for now WASHINGTON -- WASHINGTON (AP) — High gas prices are intensifying inflation and vacuuming up more of Americans' dollars, yet consumers are still digging deep to spend , powering the economy, at least for now . A slew of economic data Thursday showed that inflation accelerated last month as more expensive oil and gas began to lift prices in other parts of the economy, including shipping and warehousing, before the increases reach most Americans. Wholesale food prices jumped, which could make groceries more expensive in the months ahead. At the same time, consumers also ramped up their spending, according to data released Thursday. Though much of the increase reflected higher prices, consumer resilience is powering solid U.S. economic growth. Workers are enjoying an unusual degree of job security despite scattered layoffs, which likely encourages spending despite surveys showing that many Americans have a gloomy economic outlook. It all adds up to an economy in which people are spending money but don't feel good about it. “Consumers may have gritted their teeth and looked through higher gas prices,” said Jim Baird, chief investment officer at Plante Moran Financial Advisers. “They're not happy, but they're still spending.” A report Thursday on wholesale prices helps explain the gloom: The government's producer price index, which measures costs before they reach the consumer, jumped 6.3% in September from a year earlier, the biggest increase in nearly four years . On a monthly basis, prices soared 1.3% from August to September, powered by a 20% rise in gas prices. Higher diesel prices have made shipping more expensive because long-haul trucks and freight trains rely on the fuel. Higher transportation costs may have helped push up food costs, which rose 1.2% from August to September, the biggest monthly gain since February. The wholesale price report followed the latest consumer price figures, released Wednesday, which showed inflation rising to 3.7% in September, far above the Federal Reserve's 2% target. “The jolt to transportation prices affects every good in the economy, since inputs to manufacturing move to factories and goods at all stages of production move from producer to wholesaler to retailer by truck, train or rail,” wrote Carl Weinberg, chief economist at High Frequency Economics. “This is how increases in energy prices ‘bleed through’ to prices of core goods.” Farmers also rely on diesel to power most of their equipment, which could further push up food prices. Diesel prices averaged $6.32 a gallon nationwide Thursday, according to AAA, up from just $3.66 a year ago. Bend, Oregon, shooting: Suspect ID'd, had attended elementary school, police say Iran live updates: Trump admin prepares options, including 'mother of all bombs' Hurricane Isaias: At least 4 dead as Isaias downgraded Despite those cost pressures, retail sales rose a solid 0.8% from August, more than economists had forecast. The increase was driven by a 6.4% jump in spending at gas stations, but consumers also spent elsewhere, including a healthy 1.1% rise at restaurants and bars. Economists say that as long as unemployment stays low and Americans continue working, spending will likely stay resilient. Hiring has been sluggish, but layoffs are also unusually low. Another report Thursday showed that the number of people seeking unemployment benefits stayed below 200,000 last week, a historically low figure. Applications for unemployment aid are a proxy for layoffs. “If the unemployment rate remains low, meaning consumers have a job, they will continue to spend, even if more cautiously and leaning increasingly on savings and credit,” Kathy Bostjancic, chief economist at Nationwide, said in an email. Many economists worry, however, that as inflation stays high, it will steadily erode Americans' spending power and start to weigh on the economy. Weekly paychecks, adjusted for inflation, actually declined in September compared with a year ago for the first time since May. And September hiring slowed to a disappointing 29,000 jobs from a revised 133,000 in August, according to the Labor Department early this month. The unemployment rate ticked higher to 4.2% from the previous month, which is still low. Yet economists had expected September payrolls to come in around 90,000. Stubbornly elevated inflation also means the Federal Reserve will likely raise its key interest rate in the coming months in an effort to slow spending and bring down inflation. When the Fed raises its rate, that can raise borrowing costs for mortgages, car loans, and credit cards over time. According to minutes released from the most recent meeting, most Fed officials expect that another interest rate increase will likely be needed this year to combat inflation.

events.title: US retail trade group forecasts healthy holiday sales, in part due to inflation
events.summary: Don’t underestimate U.S. shoppers when it comes to shelling out money for the winter holidays NEW YORK -- Don't count out U.S. shoppers when it comes to shelling out money for the winter holidays despite higher fuel prices and other financial pressures. The nation's largest retail trade group said Thursday that it expects American consumers will collectively spend $1.01 trillion this November and December, which would be 4.2% more than during the same months last year. The increase reflects more than seasonal good cheer, according to economists. The National Retail Federation and other organizations that have issued holiday forecasts said they expected higher consumer prices to account for about half of the anticipated growth. Moreover, higher income shoppers will fuel a lot of the spending, retail experts say. “We all acknowledge households continue to navigate persistent inflation and uneven confidence about the economy,” National Retail Federation President and CEO Matthew Shay told reporters on Thursday. “But throughout the year, consumers have repeatedly shown that holidays and spending on loved ones are priorities. We’re confident that pattern is going to continue through the 2026 winter holidays.” Retailers rang up $972 billion in holiday sales last year, which was 3.1% more than the year before that, the trade group said. At 4.2%, NRF's growth projection is above the actual gains from the last 20 years, which averaged 3.1% when excluding the outsized holiday spending of pandemic-era 2020 and 2021, according to Mark Mathews, the trade group's chief economist. The forecast, which was not adjusted for inflation, is in line with most other holiday predictions so far. The outlooks illustrate an ongoing disconnect between the dismal consumer confidence that shows up in monthly surveys and Americans' willingness to keep spending. The U.S. war with Iran has driven up gasoline prices for drivers and caused worries about all kinds of products getting more expensive as high diesel prices make transporting goods costlier for retailers. The average price for regular gasoline rose to $4.33 per gallon Thursday, according to motor club AAA. Before the war began, gas cost less than $3 a gallon. Experts say such higher pump prices will continue to squeeze lower-income shoppers, while higher-income shoppers buoyed by stock market gains will keep splurging on discretionary purchases. “We’ve seen disruption after disruption kind of knock people off kilter, and then the consumer comes roaring back,” Bryan Eshelman, a partner and managing director at AlixPartners, said. Instead of pulling back altogether, consumers are changing their shopping habits by trading down to lower-price brands and stores, shopping earlier and relying more on credit cards and buy now pay later plans , Eshelman said. Economists look at the holiday results as a gauge for the state of the consumer beyond the holidays. Consumer spending is monitored closely because it drives about 70% of U.S. gross domestic product. “It not only tells us about the current state of the consumer, (but) it helps inform expectations for the year ahead as well," Mastercard Economics Institute chief economist Michelle Meyer said. “It gives us a lot of incredible insights into how consumers are doing from a macro perspective.” The institute, which tracks spending across all payment methods including cash, forecast a 5.5% increase in holiday sales from Nov. 1 through Dec. 24 compared to last year. Although Mastercard estimated that half of the growth would come from higher prices instead of more sales, the institute still expects healthy spending by shoppers because of a decent U.S. job market, Meyer said. “I guess they feel some sense of security because the jobless numbers are so low," she said. events.title: Trump says Fort Hood shooter's execution will not be livestreamed
events.summary: President Trump said in a Thursday Truth Social post that the execution of the convicted Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan by firing squad will not be live-streamed. The big picture: The president's post walks back an idea that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth pitched last week, setting off an avalanche of bipartisan condemnation. Driving the news: " He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed," Trump's post read. He added, "That said, the execution may be viewed in person by the immediate families of the victims, if they so choose." Trump noted that he thinks "streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan but, many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die." That seemingly included Vice President JD Vance , who said he wouldn't watch the execution. House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) warned footage of the execution could become a "recruiting tool for future terrorists." What they're saying: Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said in a statement provided to Axios that Trump and Secretary Hegseth discussed the decision ahead of the Truth Social post. Parnell added: "The Secretary supports the President's decision, and they are completely aligned." Catch up quick: The Pentagon previously confirmed that the December execution would be streamed after Hegseth said in an interview with Real America's Voice that it would be made "public." But the plan received swift pushback from Republicans and Democrats in Congress alike, as well as from clergy and survivors of the horrific 2009 attack. Even though most Americans support executing Hasan, a vast majority oppose livestreaming his death by firing squad, according to an ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos poll out Thursday. Representatives for TikTok and Newsmax told Axios their platforms wouldn't allow execution livestreams or clips, Axios' Sara Fischer reported. Friction point: The reversal also comes after Axios' Marc Caputo reported that the president himself was privately expressing doubts about the public execution after being deluged with a chorus of negative sentiment. He was initially full-throated in his approval of the idea — but it took roughly a week for the plan to crumble. events.title: Volvo Cars and NVIDIA Expand Partnership to Advance Safe Automated Driving
events.summary: Volvo Cars today announced it is expanding its partnership with NVIDIA to unlock new levels of safety in automated driving technology in future cars from Volvo, building on the companies’ decade-long collaboration. Guided by Volvo Cars’ pioneering safety knowledge and powered by the NVIDIA Hyperion sensor and compute architecture, the technology will enable future Volvo cars to safely navigate complex real-world environments from door to door. This includes everything from highways and busy urban streets to parking scenarios. The technology will make its debut in a next-generation Volvo car as part of the company’s recently announced largest-ever product push. Volvo Cars will combine its industry-leading vehicle safety systems and engineering expertise with NVIDIA’s AI and accelerated computing technologies. These include the Hyperion sensor and compute architecture, Halos OS, and Alpamayo Stack driving software. Together, the companies will raise the bar for AI-enabled car safety while making driving feel easier and more effortless for customers, with a gradual introduction of eyes-off and mind-off driving. Volvo Cars brings nearly a century of real-world safety research and its human-centric approach to this development. The ambition is to set a new benchmark for automated driving that is safe, convenient and worthy of customer trust. “Volvo has been synonymous with car safety for almost 100 years,” said Håkan Samuelsson, president and CEO of Volvo Cars. “By working with NVIDIA, we bring together two distinct strengths: industry-leading safety knowledge and world-class AI technology. That combination gives us a unique opportunity to create safer and more attractive cars for our customers.” “Accelerated computing has transformed the car into an intelligent machine that can understand the world around it,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “Volvo has spent nearly a century protecting people on the road. Together, we’re combining Volvo’s extraordinary vehicle safety systems with NVIDIA Hyperion and Halos to build a new generation of cars that make driving safer and more effortless.” This expanded partnership marks another milestone in the companies’ long-standing collaboration, which began in 2017. Volvo Cars is bringing the industry’s most advanced computing capabilities into its next generation of electric cars, establishing it as a leader in software-defined cars. events.title: 'I paid thousands to a company for jobs that never came'
events.summary: Apurv Patel said he paid Synetal Solutions £3,600 and claimed he was verbally promised a guaranteed sponsored job A company has been accused of promising jobs in the healthcare sector which never materialised, leaving people thousands of pounds out of pocket. Registered in 2025, Synetal Solutions Ltd says it offers career-focused training programmes in the healthcare and IT sectors. But the BBC has spoken to a number of people who claim they were promised training and support to secure sponsored healthcare jobs that never became available to apply for. London Citizens Advice says it has seen an increase in recruitment-related scams since the government stopped overseas recruitment for care workers , external . The charity described the firm's practices as "unethical". Synetal Solutions says it "takes these concerns seriously and disputes the broad allegation that its services or candidate outcomes are fictitious". Apurv Patel, who has been in the UK on a Skilled Worker visa since 2023, said he paid Synetal Solutions £3,600 across February and March for healthcare training after he and a friend were verbally promised guaranteed sponsored jobs. Eight months later he has received no job offers, interviews or meaningful employment support, he said. "I'm frustrated. I paid money, I wasted my time. I did whatever they wanted without any result," he said. "It's had a miserable effect on my family and finances." Patel said he did receive some training but described it as poor quality and ultimately "worthless". Having previously worked for two years as a healthcare assistant, he said he became concerned when a trainer was unable to answer routine questions about care work. "She didn't give us any answers and we realised she didn't have any experience of healthcare," he said. The company disputes claims that training was ineffective. He also alleged communication with the company deteriorated after he made his second payment, with responses sometimes taking several days. Patel has since complained to his bank and sought help from Citizens Advice. The BBC has seen emails from the company advertising a "three-month recruitment programme" offering "training and placement with sponsorship" for £5,500. Home Office guidance , external states agencies may charge for services such as training or CV-writing assistance, but cannot charge fees solely for finding, or attempting to find, employment. Responding to questions about its marketing, Synetal Solutions said: "We acknowledge the 'guarantee' wording in the emails supplied and recognise that contractual terms alone do not resolve concerns about those assurances." As part of its programme, Synetal Solutions created accounts for trainees on iHasco, a health and social care training platform. The BBC contacted iHasco, which confirmed the company was a customer. However, it said its terms did not permit customers to resell its training content to individuals who were not employees. The company said it was reviewing Synetal Solutions' account and would take appropriate action if necessary. Synetal Solutions said it had acted in accordance with its agreement with iHasco. The Care Quality Commission said there was no single qualification that automatically qualified someone to work as a care worker. Instead, providers are responsible for ensuring employees are appropriately trained and competent for their roles. The BBC also contacted a number of healthcare organisations whose logos appeared on Synetal Solutions' website as examples of employers where graduates had worked. Those organisations that responded said they had no links to the company. Some also said they had not authorised the use of their branding, and some said they would not accept certificates provided through the company's training. Daniel Blake says the way Synetal Solutions has operated is unethical Daniel Blake, director of London Citizens Advice, described the company's approach as "exploitative". "The promises that were made are impossible promises," he said. "They are targeting people with vulnerable immigration status. "This company is asking for large sums of money upfront without any reputable standards, without any reputable evidence of success, and yet when it goes wrong they are refusing to take any responsibility. "For us, it seems a very unethical way of conducting business." He added that no reputable recruitment agency would guarantee a successful outcome without first assessing a candidate and matching them to a suitable role, and urged anybody asked to pay large sums upfront to seek independent advice. "If it seems too good to be true, it probably is," he said. The company's website stated: "Synetal Solutions provides the right support, guidance, and guaranteed job placement to help you succeed." But since the BBC contacted Synetal Solutions mentions of job guarantees were removed from the website.

events.title: Trump FDA nominee played key role in overhaul of childhood vaccine policy
events.summary: The News Heidi Overton, President Donald Trump’s nominee to run the Food and Drug Administration, played a larger role in driving the process to reduce the number of vaccines the government recommends to children than emerged during her Senate confirmation last month, when Republican senators asked her whether she’d stand up to anti-vaccine voices in the administration. An aide on the president’s Domestic Policy Council, Overton helped edit and craft a scientific justification that was used to underpin cutting the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommendations from 17 to 11 vaccines in January, according to a senior administration official and three people familiar with the process. “It was Heidi driving this whole thing,” said a former senior administration official, noting that Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. supported the policy push. The Senate health committee did not vote on whether to advance Overton to the Senate floor before departing earlier this month, leaving the decision for the lame duck session. If Republicans ultimately support her, Overton will lead the agency responsible for vaccine policy after making a bigger contribution to the Trump administration’s effort to reverse decades of American policy on childhood vaccines than was widely understood. “Every vaccine on the US market right now are safe and effective according to the FDA,” Overton told Senate Health Committee Chair Bill Cassidy, R-La, during the hearing. But throughout the fall of 2025, Overton built consensus across health agencies around narrowing the list of recommended universal childhood vaccines, meeting with Trump administration officials including Kennedy; then-FDA Commissioner Marty Makary; Mehmet Oz, who oversees Medicare and Medicaid; Jay Bhattacharya, the director of the National Institutes of Health; and Stefanie Spear, a senior HHS official and close confidant to Kennedy. Others in the administration say that Overton’s work is a reflection of the nature of a White House policy job, not her own priorities. “I think there is a misperception that because Heidi is the point of contact for the White House on a lot of issues, that she personally is doing something because of her personal views or or motivations,” a separate administration official said, noting the White House is “top-down.” The Atlantic reported in July that Overton had been part of a team that created an initial draft of childhood vaccine recommendations. Kennedy was prepared to endorse Denmark’s vaccine schedule, which recommends vaccinations against 10 diseases for all children, as an option for American parents based on the memo. But Kennedy’s December press conference was canceled at the last minute, according to three people familiar with the discussions. Before the scheduled event, HHS lawyers raised concerns to senior health officials that it lacked evidence and would be susceptible to legal challenges, two of the people said. On Jan. 5, former Health Deputy Secretary and then-acting CDC Director Jim O’Neill signed a decision memo that adopted a revised childhood immunization schedule based on the assessment conducted by Høeg, the acting director of the FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research at the time, and Martin Kulldorff, an HHS aide. The American Academy of Pediatrics challenged the revised schedule in court , and a federal judge put it on hold in March. Know More When Trump nominated Overton in August to lead the FDA, prominent Make America Healthy Again activists objected, saying she would be too friendly toward drugmakers if confirmed. “This narrative took hold that Heidi was not aligned with Kennedy on this, was more aligned with pharma [on] vaccine stuff, and was in favor of a more maximal vaccine schedule,” the former senior administration official said. “And that’s just not the case, not what happened.” An HHS official said Overton was tasked with putting Trump’s policy priority into a document that was “suitable for distribution throughout the White House.” “Someone needed to sort of pull the different strands together and make sure they came together into a quilt that was at least representative of what the different folks were trying to do,” the HHS official said. “The president had already expressed, and has continued to express a very strong desire to revisit vaccines, in part because he’s concerned about complications. This is not something that she would have personally desired. I am quite confident.” At her Senate confirmation hearing in September, Cassidy pressed Overton on her commitment to defending the safety and efficacy of vaccines, and asked whether she’d stand up to Trump under pressure. “If he asks you to do something which goes against the guarantee you’ve made to the American people through us, what will you do?” Cassidy asked. “I would give him my best advice,” Overton replied. Cassidy is a trained gastroenterologist and liver specialist who is leaving office this year after losing a primary election where Trump endorsed his challenger and has said Kennedy’s vaccine approach broke commitments made during his own confirmation process. His office declined to comment when asked about Overton’s involvement in drafting the scientific justification document. When Trump nominated Overton, Cassidy posted that her involvement in Trump’s “nonsensical vaccine executive order” in August , which aimed to break up the established measles, mumps and rubella vaccine into multiple doses, was “almost disqualifying.” Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester, D-Del., pressed Overton at the confirmation hearing about whether she thought splitting the MMR vaccine into multiple shots or reducing the number of childhood vaccines were “good options.” “My job in my current role is to take the president’s directive, provide options to him for him to make the decision,” Overton responded. Notable Overton was quiet on her own opinions during her confirmation hearing , STAT reported . If Democrats take control of the Senate next year, they’ll confirm “very few” of Trump’s nominees , Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer told Semafor’s Burgess Everett .

events.title: Perplexity to give away its AI security software
events.summary: The Scoop Perplexity is giving away the software it has been using to combat rogue AI agents, the company told Semafor Thursday. Its “AI sandbox,” which it calls SPACE, is now an open source project, allowing outside developers to use the tool, which it says can keep AI agents contained. Perplexity said it’s lined up partners, including CoreWeave, Akamai and Crusoe, which have agreed to offer SPACE to customers. Sandboxes, or isolated environments for testing and running AI models, have become a hot topic in the tech industry in the wake of reports from AI labs of models escaping their constraints, finding their way onto the open web and hacking unsuspecting victims like Hugging Face and the Australian government. While AI companies focus on “alignment,” or training models to behave themselves, the security industry has been increasingly advocating erecting strict guardrails around AI models. “A lot of companies are thinking about how to build secure AI agents, and in many cases they hit a wall,” said Zibi Braniecki, a member of the technical staff at Perplexity, in an interview with Semafor. “We have a solution.” Perplexity said it tested SPACE by giving nine frontier models instructions to try to break out. In 118 tries, none of them did, while Perplexity found they were able to break out of other sandboxes that were not open sourced. Know More Braniecki likened the effort to make SPACE open source to what happened with web browsers as the internet developed — companies came together to build guardrails that allowed secure browsing and online commerce. “Right now, we’re thinking too small,” he said. Other companies like Nvidia have also released open-source security tools, such as Nvidia OpenShell, which runs AI agents in a sandbox and limits what they can reach. Perplexity said SPACE also helps reduce wasted compute, which can be a byproduct of strict sandboxing.

events.title: "Mommy and daddy" play nice: Apple and Meta team up to bring open-source Muse to Macs
events.summary: Apple and Meta, whose leaders have spent years trading barbs over privacy and the future of computing, are joining forces to bring one of America's most powerful open-weight AI models to Apple's high-end Macs. Why it matters: The collaboration marks a striking detente between two longtime Silicon Valley rivals, underscoring how the AI race is reshaping relationships across the technology industry. The companies still compete over devices and the next generation of computing, but both see an opportunity in bringing powerful AI capabilities to personal computers. "We're excited for mommy and daddy to be playing nice again," Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang told Axios. Driving the news: Meta is releasing Muse Spark Open, a model similar to Muse Spark 1.3 that it says is the most powerful U.S.-developed open-weight AI model available. Meta joins a host of Western AI companies that have released powerful open-weight systems that promise to slash AI costs, provide companies with more control and offer an alternative to the Chinese AI ecosystem. Nvidia on Tuesday released updated versions of its Nemotron family of models, and U.S.-based Reflection AI and France's Mistral both released new open-source models last week. As proof of Muse Spark Open's capabilities, Meta worked with Apple to make the model run locally across two or four connected Mac Studios powered by Apple's M5 Ultra chips, using Apple's MLX framework. Zoom in: The prospect of a powerful model — it has 816 billion parameters — running on Apple hardware offers a proof of concept for how companies could build their own AI systems. That could give companies more alternatives to Nvidia GPUs and proprietary models from leading AI companies, potentially shifting some of the economics of AI. Meta's model will be free to download, with a license allowing commercial use, and will also be available through cloud providers and developer tools. What they're saying: Wang said the companies have been working together for several months, with Daniel Gross, a former Apple executive now at Meta, helping bring the two sides together. "I think he played a really big role in kind of getting the two companies to work nicely together," Wang said in a telephone interview. Flashback: Apple executive chairman Tim Cook and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg have repeatedly clashed over privacy and their competing business models. In 2018, amid Facebook's Cambridge Analytica scandal, Cook was asked what he would do if he were Zuckerberg. "I wouldn't be in this situation," Cook replied. Zuckerberg called Cook's comments "extremely glib." The rivalry intensified in 2021, when Apple introduced new privacy protections that struck at the heart of Facebook's ad business. Zuckerberg reportedly told employees that Facebook needed to "inflict pain" on Apple over the dispute, according to the Wall Street Journal. The big picture: The AI race is making for some strange bedfellows, scrambling long-standing Silicon Valley rivalries and even bringing together political adversaries. Anthropic is leasing up to $15 billion per year of computing capacity from Elon Musk's SpaceX, even as it competes with his AI company. Microsoft, OpenAI's longtime partner, is investing billions in rival Anthropic and incorporating its Claude models into its own products. And in Washington, progressive Sen. Bernie Sanders and MAGA strategist Steve Bannon have found common ground in calling for tougher AI safeguards and challenging the power of Big Tech. Between the lines: The Apple-Meta collaboration doesn't mean the companies have resolved their differences, but it suggests those disagreements no longer prevent them from working together when their interests align. Meta benefits from making its AI models widely available, while Apple can showcase the capabilities of its most powerful computers. And because the model runs locally, Meta doesn't receive users' prompts or other information — sidestepping the privacy concerns that have long divided the companies. "Meta has no control or visibility to any of that," Wang said of how developers use the model. Yes, but: Making powerful AI models openly available raises concerns that bad actors could remove safeguards and use the technology for cyberattacks or biological threats. What we're watching: Whether the collaboration marks the beginning of a broader relationship between Apple and Meta. For now, Apple is helping demonstrate that Meta's AI models can run locally on its computers. A more significant step would be Apple incorporating Meta's models into Apple Intelligence, giving the Facebook parent a role in powering Apple's own AI features. The bottom line: Wang acknowledged that Apple and Meta will continue to compete in some areas, but said that doesn't have to prevent them from working together. "Where it makes sense to collaborate and partner, we want to be able to do so," he said.

events.title: Adobe and NVIDIA Expand Collaboration to Speed Agentic Creation
events.summary: News Summary: Adobe is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA to optimize its flagship tools including Adobe Photoshop, Premiere, Substance 3D, Frame.io and Brand Concierge, delivering faster AI-powered creation, production and personalization. Adobe is bringing the power of the NVIDIA RTX Spark superchip to its agentic creative applications Photoshop, Premiere and Substance 3D. Optimized to take full advantage of RTX Spark, these applications deliver up to 2x faster AI processing, editing, color and effects, helping creatives iterate faster and stay in their creative flow. Adobe Brand Concierge is now optimized with NVIDIA Nemotron open models, providing enterprises a flexible and efficient way to deliver high-quality conversational experiences at scale, with NVIDIA also selecting Brand Concierge to power relevant and contextual customer interactions on NVIDIA.com. Adobe (Nasdaq: ADBE), the global technology leader that unleashes creativity, productivity and customer experiences through innovative tools and platforms, and NVIDIA today announced an expansion of their partnership to optimize Adobe’s flagship tools including Adobe Photoshop, Premiere, Substance 3D, Frame.io and Brand Concierge, delivering faster AI-powered creation, production and personalization. This work builds on Adobe and NVIDIA’s strategic partnership announced in March, which brings together Adobe’s creative and marketing workflows, models and technology with NVIDIA’s open models, libraries, research and accelerated computing to accelerate creative, production and marketing workflows across video, images, 3D and other creative media. That collaboration includes GPU acceleration for media ingestion and intelligence in Frame.io, as well as ongoing work around Adobe Substance 3D, Adobe Firefly Foundry and 3D digital twin workflows for enterprise customers. “Creative workflows are more multimodal than ever, with many projects spanning images, video, audio, motion and 3D, making performance critical to helping creatives stay focused on their ideas and craft,” said Deepa Subramaniam, vice president, product marketing, creative professionals, Adobe. “By partnering with NVIDIA to optimize Photoshop, Premiere and Substance 3D for RTX Spark and accelerating Frame.io in the cloud, we’re delivering the performance creatives need to bring their ideas to life.” “AI agents are helping creators unlock deeper and richer workflows using the Adobe applications they know and love,” said Jason Paul, vice president, local AI, NVIDIA. “Powered by RTX Spark, Adobe’s optimized tools deliver up to 2x faster performance to accelerate these new workflows.”   Empowering Creatives With Faster Adobe Tools Rearchitected With NVIDIA Creative professionals today move between image, video, motion and 3D, sometimes all within the same project. As AI increasingly becomes part of the creative process, they need technology that keeps pace with the speed of their ideas and the complexity of their workflows. As an industry leader in creativity, Adobe’s tools apply decades of creative expertise to amplify human potential and make it easier to quickly turn ideas into impactful work. Adobe is bringing the power of the NVIDIA RTX Spark superchip, launching tomorrow, Oct. 16, to its agentic creative applications Photoshop , Premiere and Substance 3D . RTX-accelerated and optimized to take full advantage of RTX Spark’s unified memory and AI compute, these applications deliver up to 2x faster AI processing, editing, color and effects, helping creatives iterate faster and stay in their creative flow. Adobe rearchitected Photoshop around GPU-accelerated compositing to be faster and more responsive for creative tasks from removing distractions with the Remove Tool to applying effects like Gaussian Blur and Light Leaks directly on canvas. Some of the most demanding post-production workflows in Premiere, from playback and rendering to effects, color and AI-powered tools, are RTX-accelerated and optimized for RTX Spark. This results in real, tangible speed gains for popular audio and video features in Premiere like Enhance Speech and Object Mask. For 3D artists using Substance 3D Painter, RTX Spark speeds up the heaviest steps around texturing. Accelerating Cloud Video Workflows With Frame.io and NVIDIA Adobe is also using NVIDIA accelerated computing to speed cloud media processing and intelligent content discovery for Adobe Frame.io , helping production teams find and use growing media libraries faster. The updated Frame.io pipeline uses NVIDIA video acceleration, including NVIDIA NVDEC for hardware-accelerated decoding and NVIDIA TensorRT ™ with CUDA ®   for content preprocessing and embedding generation. Moving compute-intensive video decoding, preprocessing and embedding generation onto NVIDIA GPUs lets Frame.io process media faster and make it searchable sooner, while supporting more responsive discovery across large content libraries.   Early performance results from selected Frame.io transcode and search workloads show: Approximately 5x faster embedding generation 4-5x improvement in P95 processing latency An approximately 80% smaller search proxy For creative teams, these gains mean uploaded content becomes searchable sooner, larger libraries refresh more efficiently, and discovery and review stay frictionless as media volumes grow. Personalized Conversational Experiences With Adobe Brand Concierge Optimized on NVIDIA Nemotron Brands also want more choice and value from the AI models powering personalized experiences. Open models can help meet that need, providing a flexible and efficient way to deliver high-quality, responsive conversations at enterprise scale. Adobe and NVIDIA worked together to optimize Brand Concierge using NVIDIA Nemotron™ open models. This version will be available to enterprise customers later this year. NVIDIA has also selected Brand Concierge to drive personalized conversational experiences grounded in organizational data and content. This enables NVIDIA to tailor interactions on their website based on customer needs, while leveraging Nemotron to deliver fast, high-quality responses at scale. Sparking Creativity, to the MAX Get ready for what’s next — with three days of creative skill-building, visionary keynotes and valuable connections at Adobe MAX , running Nov. 10-12. Adobe and NVIDIA will showcase the latest advancements for creators alongside their hardware partners. ]]>

events.title: Windows 11 gets faster, more connected and easier to use
events.summary: What’s new in Windows 11: Everyday experiences, reimagined Every day, your PC helps you get things done, stay connected, capture ideas and make time for what you enjoy. That’s why Windows 11 continues to evolve, starting with a faster, more dependable and refined experience. Throughout the year, we’ve worked with the Windows Insider community on improvements to Windows that are now beginning to roll out broadly, with more to come. That same care shapes our latest Windows experiences, building on these foundational improvements with new possibilities that make everyday moments on your PC simpler and more intuitive. From new features for gamers, to a modernized Photos experience, to more seamless phone to PC integration, Windows is built to support the way you work, create, play and connect. A faster, more responsive Windows experience Responsiveness shapes nearly every experience on your PC. It’s the difference between staying in your flow and waiting for your device to catch up. That’s why we’ve continued to invest across Windows , from the platform and shell to the apps people use every day, to make Windows feel faster, more responsive and more efficient. The result is a Windows experience that’s up to 20% more responsive , with improvements you can feel as soon as you boot into your PC and extending to Start, File Explorer, Search, Snipping Tool, Microsoft 365, Edge and more 1 . A big part of that work is making smarter use of memory and system resources. We’ve improved memory management and efficiency across Windows to help keep more of your PC’s resources focused on what you’re actively doing. That work can make an especially meaningful difference on PCs with 8GB of memory. Windows can now keep up to 2GB more of your active data in memory instead of moving it to slower storage, helping your PC stay responsive as you open more apps or browser tabs. Windows is also making additional memory-saving improvements that reduce background memory use. For example, on PCs with 8GB of memory or less, Widgets load only when you open them, making more than 200 MB of memory available for your apps and other work 2 . It’s one example of the broader work underway to reduce the Windows memory footprint and deliver a fast, responsive experience across the PCs people use every day, an area we’ve made an explicit focus for Windows. But a great Windows experience isn’t only about speed. It’s also about making your PC feel dependable, less disruptive and more your own. We’re giving you more flexibility to personalize Start and your taskbar , including choosing where it appears on your screen, while making Widgets cleaner and quieter so you have more control over what gets your attention. And we’ve improved Windows Update to give you greater control over when updates happen and better coordinate updates to reduce restarts, while continuing to reduce the time it takes to apply an update. We’re also improving the everyday interactions you depend on. Bluetooth headphones work more reliably on Windows, with smoother pairing, reconnection, audio and calls, including an AirPods pairing experience that’s up to 15 seconds faster 3 . And we’ve made signing in with Windows Hello easier, faster and more reliable, with improvements to both face and fingerprint recognition. Alongside that work, we’re partnering with our hardware ecosystem through the Driver Quality Initiative to improve driver stability, reliability, security and performance across Windows devices. The result is a Windows experience that feels faster, more responsive and more thoughtfully designed around you, whether you’re opening an app, finding a file, connecting your headphones, arranging your taskbar the way you want or simply getting back to what you were doing. For hundreds of millions of people each day, Windows search on the taskbar is where intent begins. It’s one of the quickest ways to get started, whether finding a file, opening an app, or changing a setting. This release builds on the search quality improvements we delivered in recent months, with clearer results and more control over suggestions. Now, we are carrying those improvements forward with a new interface and expanding search from a place for finding information into a place for getting things done. Finding the right result is often only the first step. After finding what you’re looking for, you often need to navigate to another destination to complete the task. Actions allow you to complete common Windows tasks directly from the search results. When searching for a system setting like dark mode or night light, you can now make the relevant change without opening Settings or searching for the right sub-menu. Search can also help with managing your workspace, like minimizing or arranging open windows, and coming soon, the ability to interact with your connected phone. These actions are designed to make common tasks faster and more intuitive: simply search and act directly from the taskbar. The new Windows Search experience is available to Windows Insiders today and will roll out more broadly later this year. Learn more about the new Windows Search experience . Move between your phone and PC seamlessly When you’re in the middle of something on your PC, your phone’s messages, apps and files should be within reach too. Windows 11 brings more of your phone experience to your desktop, so you can reply to a message, answer phone calls, open apps, and keep going without reaching for another device 4 . Preview messages and notifications from your Android phone or iPhone in Start to see what needs your attention. When a conversation needs a reply, open it in a window focused on your chat, send your response and get back to what you were doing. Quick Settings keeps useful phone controls close, whether you want to silence or ring a misplaced phone. With a supported Android phone, open your phone apps in separate, resizable windows on your desktop, with room to work on the larger screen alongside your other apps. Browse your phone files in File Explorer and open what you need without switching devices. And when you take a photo on your phone, a notification on your PC lets you open it with one click, ready for a closer look. When you do move between devices, Resume helps you pick up supported activities where you left off instead of finding your place again. It’s your phone and PC working together, so you can stay connected from the screen you’re already using. Spend less time searching for your photos and more time enjoying them. The new Microsoft Photos app brings images from your PC and connected libraries into one fast, beautiful Gallery, with more of your collection in view. Whether you’re revisiting a favorite trip or browsing everyday snapshots, it’s easier to see what you have and rediscover moments worth keeping close. Find a favorite by describing it in your own words or bring memories together in albums to share.

events.title: What will the next generation of developers do when AI writes the code?
events.summary: Microsoft and Carnegie Mellon University are betting that the junior developers we train today will be the senior engineers of tomorrow. When AI can produce code in seconds, what is the job of a software engineer? For someone graduating with a computer science degree, what is the future of your daily work if it’s not coding? And when AI is designing the architecture, writing the code, and fixing the problems, how does a software engineer learn software engineering? Microsoft and Carnegie Mellon University are betting that the career of a software developer is here to stay—and that the junior developers we train today will be the senior engineers of tomorrow. That’s why we launched PRAISE: an internal preceptorship program that pairs junior engineers early in their careers with senior engineering preceptors. PRAISE stands for Preceptorship for AI-accelerated Software Engineering. We borrow the preceptorship concept from nursing, where new nurses are paired with experienced nurses to build real-world experience and confidence. The goal isn’t to keep newcomers coding as though AI never arrived. It is to help them develop the understanding, confidence, and accountability to build in the new ways we’re all learning in real-time. The partnership links practical engineering experience with academic instruction, rather than asking either academic institutions or companies to solely carry the responsibility of training the next generation of engineers. Does a CS degree matter anymore? Yes, it does People asking if software engineering degrees still matter when AI can code—and any human can use prompts to build an app—are asking the wrong question. Would these same people ship AI code in a finished product sight unseen (please, we implore you, say no)? Of course we need junior software engineers. Senior engineers ensure the technology we ship works safely and effectively, and today’s junior engineers will be tomorrow’s senior engineers. Coding with AI is only one part of the evolving software development lifecycle. More of our time is now spent on design and architecture than coding every line. But that doesn’t change the need for us to understand what the underlying code does, even if we’re not writing all of it by hand. After all, when a car breaks down, it takes someone who knows what’s going on under the hood to get it back on the road. With PRAISE, preceptors coach their preceptees to use AI tools thoughtfully, while building strong systems thinking, taste, and judgement. Just as we evolved and abstracted certain elements of software engineering by using compilers, engineers are now adapting to using AI where it provides efficiency in the overall process of creating a product. AI changes the work; it does not remove human responsibility for outcomes. Preparing the next generation of engineers means giving them access to both AI tools and experienced guides, so they can grow from producing code to deciding what deserves to be built in the first place. How the preceptor and preceptee model works What does the PRAISE model look like in the workplace? Similarly to the nursing model of preceptorship, the key is creating space for junior engineers to workshop questions and problems with senior engineers. Senior engineers need to understand that their junior team members might not always have the confidence to contribute to projects at the speed and scale possible after years in the industry. Building that confidence and rapport with their preceptor gives junior engineers room to learn by doing—not simply watching someone else solve problems. The preceptor also shares their insights, explains their taste and approach to solving a problem, and provides tips with examples. They can also advise the preceptees on where to focus based on their skills and knowledge. We teach junior engineers to test assumptions and discuss unfamiliar changes with their colleagues. Mentorship helps turn the process of producing a solution into deliberate learning. That judgement for when to use AI should be viewed as ongoing education, which is why we’re partnering with Carnegie Mellon University on curriculum as part of the PRAISE program. The intent is to set students up for success in the workplace and accelerate preceptees with formal curricula to complement the guidance from the preceptor on how to build and deliver with confidence. The courses give them early experiences in how to deploy production-ready solutions. Preceptees will take classes and participate in small group discussions to bridge theoretical concepts of computer science to real-world software engineering practices and their work at Microsoft. The curriculum at Carnegie Mellon University augments the on-the-job learning that engineers get at Microsoft from their teams and preceptors, adding formal classroom education to their training. “It used to be that early-career software engineers would do a lot of tasks that would build up their expertise,” said Michael Hilton, Teaching Professor & Associate Department Head for Education in the Software and Societal Systems Department at Carnegie Mellon University’s Kenneth C. Griffin School of Computer Science. “Combining forces between academics and practitioners allows us to bring our expertise together and create solutions that draw on computer science research while standing up to the daily realities of software development.” We’re excited to work with Carnegie Mellon University to train the next generation of software engineers, helping to maintain a healthy talent pipeline for the future workforce. LLM-as-translator pattern: Adding natural language understanding to an existing system without rewriting it Modernizing an existing implementation can be expensive and disruptive. Instead, consider introducing an abstraction layer to give your legacy system a modern facelift. Designing product simplicity for the AI era

events.title: Average long-term US mortgage rate holds at 7.4%, remaining at highest level in nearly 3 years
events.summary: Mortgage rates held steady this week, keeping the average long-term U.S. home loan rate at its highest level in nearly three years Mortgage rates held steady this week, keeping the average long-term U.S. home loan rate at its highest level in nearly three years. The benchmark 30-year fixed-rate mortgage was unchanged from last week at 7.40%, mortgage buyer Freddie Mac said Thursday. One year ago, the average rate was 6.27%. The latest reading ends a seven-week climb for the average rate, which is at the highest level since Nov. 16, 2023, when it was at 7.44%. Meanwhile, borrowing costs on 15-year fixed-rate mortgages, often sought by borrowers refinancing a home loan, eased this week. That average rate dropped to 6.71% from 6.73% last week. A year ago, it was at 5.52%. Rates on home loans are influenced by inflation, Federal Reserve policy and bond-market investors’ expectations for the economy, among other factors. They generally follow the trajectory of the 10-year Treasury yield, which lenders use as a guide to pricing home loans. Mortgage rates have been climbing since late February, when the U.S. war with Iran began , pushing up the price of oil and driving inflation higher . The run-up in rates also reflects heightened bond market volatility, which has pushed up yields on U.S. Treasurys. U.S. home sales remain stalled this year in large part because of rising mortgage rates, which can add hundreds of dollars a month in costs for borrowers, limiting homebuyers’ purchasing power and prompting many to put off buying a home. US retail trade group forecasts healthy holiday sales, in part due to inflation CDC lags in hiring behind other health agencies after DOGE cuts, union says Chile president makes first state visit to Bolivia in 71 years as region shifts right The recent string of mortgage rate increases snapped as the 10-year Treasury yield pulled back from its highest level since 2002. The yield was at 5.10% at midday Thursday on the bond market. It had topped 5.30% earlier this month amid worries about high inflation, signals of a strong U.S. economy and other factors. It’s still well above its 3.97% level from before the war with Iran began. In late February, the average rate on a 30-year mortgage briefly dipped to 5.98%, its lowest level going back to late 2022. The 1.42 percentage point increase in the rate since then translates roughly into an additional monthly cost of $376 for a borrower financing a $400,000 home loan at the current average rate. Depending on a borrower’s income, credit and other factors, they may qualify for a rate on a 30-year mortgage that is below or above the current average. The U.S. housing market has been in a slump since 2022, when mortgage rates began to climb from pandemic-era lows. Sales of previously occupied U.S. homes were essentially flat last year, stuck at a 30-year low. This week, the National Association of Realtors said that existing U.S. home sales rose in September from the previous month, but slowed compared to a year earlier amid rising mortgage rates and home prices. events.title: BBC asks judge to force Trump to sit for deposition in his own lawsuit against the channel
events.summary: Lawyers for the BBC say that President Donald Trump is trying to delay sitting for a deposition in the defamation case he brought against the British broadcaster until January 2027 NEW YORK -- Lawyers for the BBC say President Donald Trump is trying to delay sitting for a deposition in the defamation case he brought against the British broadcaster until January 2027. In a filing this week , they asked a Florida court to compel the president to appear in the $10 billion case after they say he canceled an agreed-upon date this week, citing “matters of national importance.” “Two months of discovery remaining, the BBC still has not been able to depose, and does not even have a schedule to depose, the most central figure in this case: Plaintiff himself," attorney Charles D. Tobin wrote in the filing. “Those delays have flouted the cooperative spirit of discovery and precluded the BBC from obtaining the evidence necessary to robustly litigate its defense.” Trump, who has a history of avoiding depositions, filed the lawsuit against the BBC last December, seeking $10 billion in damages as he accused the British broadcaster of defamation as well as deceptive and unfair trade practices related to a documentary, “Trump: A Second Chance.” Britain’s publicly funded national broadcaster admitted filmmakers spliced together quotes from different sections of the speech Trump delivered to his supporters on Jan. 6, 2021, before the storming of the U.S. Capitol, to make it seem like he was directly urging violence. The 33-page lawsuit accused the BBC of broadcasting a “false, defamatory, deceptive, disparaging, inflammatory, and malicious depiction of President Trump,” calling it “a brazen attempt to interfere in and influence” the 2024 U.S. presidential election. The broadcaster apologized to Trump over the edit and the head of the BBC and the British broadcaster’s top news executive both resigned. But the broadcaster has denied Trump's claims that it defamed him. Bend, Oregon, shooting: Suspect ID'd, had attended elementary school, police say 2 women found dead in suitcases leads to multistate hunt for killer Atlanta school worker dies after falling from Six Flags roller coaster in Georgia In the filing this week, BBC lawyers said that they first requested dates for the deposition in July, and followed up repeatedly. Both sides, they said, eventually agreed on Oct. 16. However, after weeks of silence, they wrote, “Plaintiff’s counsel responded on September 28, 2026, indicating that ‘the President is no longer available for his deposition on October 16 due to other matters of national importance’ and that counsel would ‘endeavor to provide you with a replacement date by the end of this week.’ He did not.” Instead, they said, they were told last week that Trump “has no availability whatsoever for a deposition" before discovery is set to close on Dec. 18. and were told that Trump would instead make himself available the second or third week of January. In a statement in response to the filing, a spokesperson for Trump’s legal team did not address the reasons for Trump's delay, but repeated its allegations against the BBC and said the president was holding the broadcaster “accountable for its defamation and reckless election interference just as he has held other fake news mainstream media responsible for their wrongdoing.” Trump voluntarily dropped a $500 million lawsuit he filed against his former lawyer and fixer Michael Cohen in 2023, days before he was set to give a deposition in that suit. events.title: IEA oil supply pledge to exceed target as it boosts release of remaining stocks
events.summary: The International Energy Agency (IEA) has said that its March pledge to release crude oil stocks will exceed its target, and will be accelerating the release of the remaining supplies as global efforts to tame soaring energy prices continue. Members of the Paris-based agency have so far released 330 million barrels of oil, and the remaining 100 million barrels – which includes more than 20 million barrels of diesel – will be released in a “timely manner consistent with national circumstances”, it said in a statement on Thursday. That would make the total releases exceed the initial 400 million barrels the IEA had pledged in March, at the onset of the war between US and Israel and Iran. “Some IEA members have released higher volumes than initially pledged in March while other members intend to do so,” the IEA said after a meeting. Specific plans are already in place ... [to release the stocks] as soon as possible.” Global energy prices remain volatile and elevated as the war in Iran, now in its eighth month, continues to choke energy supplies. Earlier this month, G7 leaders pledged to accelerate the IEA's co-ordinated emergency stock release by rolling out 100 million barrels of diesel and other reserves through the IEA to help to stabilise markets. And in a surprising move last week, US President Donald Trump's administration lifted sanctions on Russia to enable the latter to supply millions of barrels of diesel to global markets. The Opec + group, meanwhile, kept its oil production targets unchanged for November, extending the pause it started in October after six months of gradual increases. Oil prices rose after the IEA's announcement. Brent, the benchmark for two-thirds of the world's oil, added 0.15 per cent to $106.20 a barrel at 8.27pm UAE time. West Texas Intermediate, the gauge that tracks US crude, jumped 3.28 per cent to $98.21 a barrel. Thursday's IEA statement said it has “encouraged those IEA members holding oil production and refining capacities to boost supply of crude and refined products, particularly diesel”. The IEA said it will continue to monitor the progress of the completion of its March pledge, “and will inform G7 leaders as requested and the IEA governing board on further actions needed, based on an updated oil market assessment, focusing on diesel”, it added.

events.title: The too-hot-for-comfort economy
events.summary: Data: Bureau of Labor Statistics; Chart: Courtenay Brown/Axios Data this week has all told the same story: This is a rip-roaring U.S. economy with all the inflationary pressures that might imply. The big picture: It puts Warsh and the Fed in a difficult jam. Top officials have signaled patience in further interest rate hikes in recent weeks, but the latest data implies broader inflationary pressures than previously thought, testing that conviction. There is scant evidence that price pressures are receding on their own and growing reason to fear that they are becoming more entrenched, which could compel a more aggressive rate-hiking response. Driving the news: On Thursday the government said the Producer Price Index rose 1.3% in September, the highest since 2022 and far above the 0.6% analysts expected. It came on the heels of a too-hot-for-comfort reading on consumer prices Wednesday. Also Thursday, September retail sales notched a 0.8% rise, versus the 0.4% analysts had expected. And the August number was revised higher. There were only 199,000 initial claims for unemployment benefits last week, remaining near historic lows. Between the lines: The U.S. growth juggernaut shows no sign of diminishing — but neither do the price pressures that have bedeviled the economy for nearly five consecutive years. If anything, the PPI and CPI data released this week suggest inflation is broadening, showing up in sectors well beyond energy. State of play: In his appearance at the International Monetary Fund's meetings in Thailand Friday (11:30pm ET Thursday), Warsh has a final opportunity to comment before the Fed enters its customary quiet period in advance of a policy meeting that concludes Oct. 28. Colleagues including New York Fed president John Williams and vice chair Philip Jefferson gave rather clear signaling in the last couple of weeks that they see little urgency to raise rates at a second consecutive meeting this month. Warsh faces a dilemma. If he affirms that stance in spite of the hot price data, it could raise doubts about his determination to bring inflation under control. If he seems inclined to raise rates, he could seem overly reactive to a couple of economic releases, contrary to his stated goal of making the Fed less "data-point dependent." The intrigue: Surprisingly, bond yields are down Thursday despite the hot PPI number — and a surge in yields following the CPI number Wednesday mostly reversed later in the trading session. It seems to reflect a flight to quality among traders as optimism around the AI buildout fades. With semiconductor and related stocks down, money looks to be flowing into safer Treasury securities. The policy-sensitive two-year Treasury yield briefly touched 4.95% after the CPI number Wednesday, implying significant Fed rate hikes ahead. It was down to 4.72% Thursday morning — an astonishing move for any 24-hour period, let alone one that included hotter-than-expected inflation data. What they're saying: "Today's September PPI report reinforces Wednesday's CPI message that inflation is turning higher and moving in the wrong direction for the Fed," Nationwide financial market economist Oren Klachkin wrote in a note. "AI continues to lend upside pressure from categories directly and indirectly tied to the buildout. Businesses seem to be passing higher costs onto customers as the proxy for margins rose heftily in September."

events.title: Missed a lecture? This AI agent at Bar-Ilan University helps students catch up
events.summary: When Yarden Shay missed some classes in her first semester at Bar-Ilan University (BIU) last year, she struggled to get up to speed. The lectures were on legal responsibility, just one of 22 modules in the first year of her undergraduate degree in criminology and psychology. Plugging that knowledge gap with borrowed notes while staying on top of six to eight hours of fresh lectures daily was an ordeal, she recalls. “It’s like a gap that is growing through time,” says Shay. “So, you’re already falling behind, and you’re getting new information that isn’t connecting, because you don’t have the previous information. The stress is everywhere.” That stress is less an issue for her today. Yarden Shay, an undergraduate at Bar-Ilan University (BIU) who is studying for a degree in criminology and psychology. Photo by Yarden Lev for Microsoft. In February, BIU piloted an AI agent on its Moodle learning platform that helps students search and summarize course materials using natural language queries, turning these vast resources into learning support. Powered by Azure AI Services and developed by KPMG and OpenApp using Microsoft Copilot Studio , the agent is grounded exclusively in course materials uploaded by BIU’s teaching staff, including recorded lectures, transcripts, presentations and articles. Students can ask the agent to zero in on a topic mentioned in a lecture, create summaries and even test them using the quiz feature. The pilot covered 71 courses and about 2,400 students at BIU, one of Israel’s leading public research universities with over 20,000 students in Ramat Gan, near Tel Aviv. Available in Hebrew, Arabic and English, the agent will be rolled out to another 100 courses in the first semester of the 2026/27 academic year, which began in October. The agent operates in the university’s secure Microsoft Azure environment. For Shay, having all that information organized and uploaded in one place means she no longer spends hours tracking down her course mates for missing notes. But the AI agent — represented by a blue robotic owl — is not just a means of catching up. She now uses it as a study aid. “The AI tool takes notes of everything, including the lectures. And I prefer reading the notes because I can’t ask questions during the lecture, and this way I feel like my brain is working,” she says. “I need active study, and that’s what the AI tool is doing. Because it gives you everything you need to know and a way of testing yourself about what you’ve learned.” Photo by Ron Rahamim for Microsoft. Shay gets the learning agent to test her, using both the multiple-choice format as well as open-ended questions. It tells her when she’s got an answer right or wrong and why. She now spends about three hours a day studying after lectures, compared with five to six hours previously. Having the AI tool as her study companion, she says, has made her feel more self-reliant and improved her student experience. And she can now share her own notes, created with the AI agent’s help. “A few students asked me for my summaries, and it felt so good that they had helped me, and I can now help them,” she says. AI as teacher’s assistant, not replacement Eliyahu Biton, a practicing lawyer and lecturer at BIU since 2017, helped test the AI agent before it went live. His priority, he says, was getting the agent to perform well enough to be his teaching assistant. This meant overhauling and updating materials for the online healthcare law and ethics courses he runs for medical imaging students every year. Eliyahu Biton, a lecturer at BIU, left, and student Yarden Shay . Photo by Ron Rahamim for Microsoft. “If you want the bot to be grounded in the material, you need to explain it because you want it to teach what you want to teach,” he says. “So, I needed to rephrase the course materials and get detailed papers for it. If I want it to be my assistant, I need to teach it. So, I teach the bot what to learn, what to answer the students.” Oversight of the course materials is essential to ensure they can be relied on by the students as learning aids. This included feeding the AI agent transcripts of all his video lectures and expanding the bullet points on his slides with research papers and recommended reading. Then he painstakingly tested the agent’s responses until he was satisfied with their accuracy. So far, he has observed positive changes in his students since the AI learning tool was introduced. He says he fields fewer routine and administrative questions, and students are less nervous about examinations. “They are more relaxed about exams now,” he says. “Before, I would just upload old exam questions for them to revise. Now I ask them to ask the bot to generate an exam for them. So, they come to the exam more relaxed because they can generate more questions and do their own exams.” At the finals in August, the average score among his 50 or so students was three percentage points higher than in previous years — an outcome he concedes could also be due to a better-than-average cohort. As part of the course, Biton continues to hold 90-minute sessions with his students four to six times a year, where he picks a topic from the course for a deeper discussion. He notes, however, that his role is transforming from pure teaching to mentoring now that the learning agent makes it easier to find course information. “Knowledge is no longer the problem,” he says, referring to how quickly AI can retrieve that information. “But what I can do better than a chatbot is to mentor, to guide the student on how to learn and how to approach challenges in the real world.” For Shay, the AI agent is an add-on, not a replacement for her teachers. “It’s something that you build on, and then you get a better understanding of the course,” she says. “So it’s something that goes with the lecturer, not instead of the lecturer.” Top Image: BIU is one of Israel’s leading public research universities. It introduced the learning agent in 71 courses and plans to expand it to another 100 courses. Photo by Ron Rahamim for Microsoft.

events.title: DOJ gave California a voter list, a 48-hour deadline — and a threat of court action
events.summary: The Trump administration is threatening emergency court action unless California officials investigate potential ineligible voters within 48 hours and set aside ballots from anyone whose citizenship they cannot verify, according to two letters sent to state officials from the Justice Department. Why it matters: With voting already underway, President Trump 's DOJ could delay ballots from eligible Californians mistakenly flagged as noncitizens and set up a court fight just three weeks before Election Day. Driving the news: Acting Deputy Attorney General R. Trent McCotter sent a letter Tuesday to Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk Dean Logan along with a thumb drive of "likely noncitizens who were sent a vote-by-mail ballot," according to a copy of the letter shared with Axios. McCotter asks local officials to investigate their citizenship status by noon October 15. The letter did not say how many people are on the list. For anyone whose status can't be confirmed, DOJ asks the officials to "segregate—not cancel" those ballots and suspend signature verification or counting of any ballots already returned. DOJ also asks officials to withhold ballots from people on the list unless their citizenship has been confirmed. California Secretary of State Shirley Weber received a similar letter . Friction point: McCotter closed his letter with a threat: "If you cannot implement this process by then, given the ongoing federal election, the United States will have no choice but to seek emergency relief." What they're saying: "This should not be controversial, as the criminal statute is clear: only American citizens may vote in federal elections. It is a federal crime for noncitizens to vote in U.S. elections, and the DOJ is asking California to ensure that is not occurring," a DOJ spokesperson said in a statement. California Secretary of State Shirley Weber said in a statement that the DOJ's "relentless efforts to unlawfully gain access to states' protected voter data and purge voter rolls serve only to cause chaos and fuel public distrust in our elections." She added that "California has robust state law requirements that only U.S. citizens can register to vote and that any non-eligible registrants are removed from the State's voter rolls." The Los Angeles County office did not respond to request for comment. The other side: "One must question why the Justice Department would violate its own rules about investigating elections so close to Election Day, particularly when their past claims have been full of errors," said David Becker, executive director of the nonpartisan Center for Election Innovation & Research, in a statement. Becker added that the administration could have investigated California's voter rolls long before mail-in ballots began going out Oct. 5. The big picture: The demand escalates the administration's push to uncover suspected noncitizen voters. In July, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin alleged more than 190,000 voters were erroneously registered in California, a claim state officials disputed. ICE investigators, FBI agents and DOJ prosecutors have dedicated significant resources to ramp up the number of cases and charges against illegal voting, with about 1,600 on-going cases as of mid-September. Yes, but: The administration's sweeping claims of mass illegal registrations and noncitizen voting have quickly deflated after inspection. After alleging 16,000 illegal registrations in Nevada, a review from state election officials saw that number dwindle to potentially 185, according to the New York Times . In Pennsylvania, DHS officials conceded it had varying degrees of confidence in the flags it made on about 14,000 voters, according to Votebeat . DHS also claimed that New Jersey had 35,000 noncitizen voters. Gov. Mike Sherril (D-NJ) did admit to mistake registrations from a software error, but the number was a fraction of DHS' claim: about 6,600 . Flashback: There have been software errors leading to registrations problems before , particularly for people using DMV services like getting a driver's license. But election experts note actual voting by noncitizens remains rare. Editor's note: This story has been updated with the California secretary of state's statement.
